title: Caching
concept: A cache keeps a copy of data closer to the reader than the source of truth, so most reads skip the slow path. The price is staleness: every write now has to reach the cache too, either by invalidating the old entry or by letting it expire, and races between reads, writes, and invalidations can leave the cache holding a value the database no longer has.

posts.title: Cache made consistent
posts.summary: TAO serves more than one quadrillion queries a day, and at a 99 percent hit rate that means over 10 trillion cache fills daily, so rare invalidation races still add up to real inconsistencies. Meta built Polaris, a service that acts like a client, checks replicas after each invalidation, and only reports anomalies a client could actually see, deferring expensive database checks so they don't overload the database. Together with tracing limited to the short window where races happen, this took TAO from six nines to ten nines of cache writes consistent within five minutes.
